_doc: Focus roster for steward-focus.yml (heartbeat scheduler, cron */10 UTC — a tick every ~10 minutes; drop to */5 to run harder). Each tick fires one improve run per enabled lane that is due AND idle: a lane fires its next batch within ~10 min of the last one finishing (skip-if-busy waits out any active slice), and a batch that died mid-way restarts on the next tick instead of stalling. Lane fields beyond enabled/everyHours (all optional): offset (which hours the cadence lands on — hourUTC % everyHours === offset, so 'align next run to 21:00' is offset = 21 % everyHours), window ([startUTC,endUTC) hour window, wraps midnight), startAt (ISO — lane sleeps until then), until (ISO — lane expires then; 'run every X until Y'), slices (1..10, default 1 — how many improve runs the lane fires IN PARALLEL each time it is due; each slice is a full separate unit of work with its own PR + smoke gate, all running at the same time). steward-focus dispatches the WHOLE BATCH in one tick (slice=1..N), and each run is told 'SLICE: k of N' so it takes the k-th topmost workable item from the app's queue rather than all N grabbing the same one (see improve.md § PARALLEL SLICES; chicago/4d additionally locks with tools/ticket.mjs claim/inflight). They no longer CHAIN one-at-a-time — that was only ever a workaround for the per-app concurrency queue cancelling the surplus, and steward-improve's group now carries the slice number so simultaneous runs are safe. A batch that outruns the hour just continues: the next tick skips an app while ANY slice is still in flight, so a lane tops up as a whole and never mid-batch. The next batch does NOT wait for a cron tick — the last slice to finish dispatches steward-focus itself, so a lane re-fires within ~a minute of going idle (GitHub throttles scheduled events badly under load, so the cron is only a backstop). Raise it to grind an app harder; hard-capped at 10 (10 concurrent agent runs on one app is a lot of tokens and a lot of open PRs for the janitor — step up gradually). Evaluated by .github/steward/schedule.mjs (the canonical logic — `node .github/steward/schedule.mjs next` previews every lane). Edit this file from the GitHub UI, any Claude session, or Manager's Fleet Ops panel — changes take effect on the next tick (~10 min), no workflow edits needed. Different apps run in parallel, and so do a lane's own slices; a lane never starts a new batch while one of its runs is still going. The `jobs` section schedules the platform-level recurring jobs with the SAME lane fields (slices excepted): fleet-improve (suite-wide steward pick), sweep-ux, sweep-tech, janitor — their standalone workflow crons are retired; this roster is the single scheduler. Per-lane `model` (optional) pins the Claude model for that lane's runs (e.g. claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5, claude-haiku-4-5); empty/absent = the fleet default, claude-opus-5 (applied in steward-improve.yml). Editable here or from Manager's Fleet Ops roster.
